# Reading the datasets into SQL

```{python}
con.execute("INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial")
```
```{python}
data_dir= Path("Data")
soil_suit_path = data_dir / "soil-suitability"
wastewater_path = data_dir/ "wastewater"
```

## Soil Suitability
### First Test file
This is to make sure everything works. after that, the same process will be applied to the remaining soil suitability files
```{python}
acrpc_path = soil_suit_path / "ACRPC_Soil_Septic.fgb"

con.execute(f"""--sql
  CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW ACRPC_Soil_Septic AS
  SELECT * FROM ST_READ('{acrpc_path}')
""")
```
now checking that this worked, and getting column names
```{python}
df = con.execute("SELECT * FROM ACRPC_Soil_Septic").df()
for col in df.columns:
  print(col)

display(df.head())
```
Columns OBJECTID_1, Shape_Length, and Shape_Area appear to have only zeros, so we will check to see if that is true.
If it is true, then those columns will be dropped from the final dataset
```{python}
print(df['OBJECTID_1'].unique())
print(df['Shape_Length'].unique())
print(df['Shape_Area'].unique())
```
Now to separate the table

`OGC_FID` will be the main hash key

There are two tables, Information and Geometry
- INFORMATION
    - main hash key: `OGC_FID`
    - goal: all of the unique information defining relating to a unique soil suitability region
- GEOMETRY
    - main hash key: `OGC_FID`
    - goal: hold the geometry data relating to the main hash key
These tables are split because of how large the geometry data is, making analysis faster if it is not needed
```{python}
info_cols = [
    "OGC_FID",
    "Suitability",
    "Jurisdiction",
    "RPC",
    "Acres"
]

geom_cols = [
    "OGC_FID",
    "geom"
]
```
Creating the info table
```{python}
info_string = ", ".join(info_cols)

con.execute(f"""--sql
  CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW info AS
  SELECT {info_string}
  FROM ACRPC_Soil_Septic
""")

info = con.execute("SELECT * FROM info").df()
display(info.head())
```
Creating the geom table
```{python}
geom_string = ", ".join(geom_cols)

con.execute(f"""--sql
  CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW geom AS
  SELECT {geom_string}
  FROM ACRPC_Soil_Septic
""")

geo = con.execute("SELECT * FROM geom").df()
geo.head()
```

### Extending the process to all soil suitability files
```{python}
soil_suit_data_paths = list(soil_suit_path.glob("*.fgb"))

for datafile_path in soil_suit_data_paths:
    table_name = datafile_path.stem
    con.execute(f"""--sql
    CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW {table_name} AS
    SELECT * FROM ST_READ('{datafile_path}')
    """)
    df = con.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {table_name}").df()

    # checking that there is no file where the three columns dropped have any unique values
    if df['OBJECTID_1'].unique() == df['Shape_Length'].unique() == df['Shape_Area'].unique() == [0]:
        print(f"the data for {table_name} has no unique values for OBJECTID_1, Shape_Length, or Shape_Area")
    else:
        print(f"the data for {table_name} has these unique values for: ")
        print(f"OBJECTID_1: {df['OBJECTID_1'].unique()}")
        print(f"Shape_Length: {df['Shape_Length'].unique()}")
        print(f"Shape_Area: {df['Shape_Area'].unique()}")

    # creating the info table
    info_string = ", ".join(info_cols)
    info_table_name = 'info_' + table_name

    con.execute(f"""--sql
      CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW {info_table_name} AS
      SELECT {info_string}
      FROM {table_name}
    """)

    info = con.execute(f"SELECT * FROM {info_table_name}").df()

    # creating the geom table
    geom_string = ", ".join(geom_cols)
    geom_table_name = 'geom_' + table_name

    con.execute(f"""--sql
      CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW {geom_table_name} AS
      SELECT {geom_string}
      FROM {table_name}
    """)
```
creating a color table for fill colors
```{python}
con.execute(f"""--sql
CREATE TABLE soil_suitability_type_colors (
    soil_suitability   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    hex_color       TEXT NOT NULL,
    rgba            TEXT NOT NULL  -- '[255,127,14,180]' as JSON-ish text
);

INSERT INTO soil_suitability_type_colors VALUES
    ('Well Suited',         '#2ca02c', '[44, 160, 44, 180]'),
    ('Moderately Suited',   '#ffcc00', '[255, 204, 0, 180]'),
    ('Marginally Suited',   '#fd7e14', '[253, 126, 20, 180]'),
    ('Not Suited',          '#dc3545', '[220, 53, 69, 180]'),
    ('Not Rated',           '#6c757d', '[108, 117, 125, 180]');
""")
```
